headline: Liverpool rebuffs Wirtz interest as Arsenal's run ends
paragraphs: Liverpool have knocked back outside interest in Florian Wirtz, according to both BBC and Transfermarkt reporting independently of each other, with the club said to be insisting the German playmaker is not for sale. Neither outlet names which club or clubs are circling him. The pushback comes alongside separate Opta analysis debating whether Jamie Carragher's on-air criticism of Wirtz's underwhelming start at Anfield has been fair, or overblown.

Arsenal lost to Brighton this past weekend, ending an unbeaten Premier League run that had stretched back to April and included nine straight wins, according to the Guardian's post-match analysis. That result is now history; more concretely, Arsenal Women confirmed a genuine done deal, with USWNT full-back Emily Fox signing a new three-year contract that she told BBC Sport was an 'easy decision.'

Real Madrid's Madrid derby defeat was referenced on BBC's Euro Leagues podcast, though the feed carries no further detail beyond the result. Manchester City remain top of the Premier League on a perfect five-from-five record, even as Opta's data analysis flags an unusually leaky defence for a side occupying first place. Elsewhere, Sky Sports' transfer live blog floated a potential January move for Bayern Munich to sign Dani Olmo, a single-source line not corroborated elsewhere in today's feed.
